title: Untrusted Tool Output Evaluated as Code Downstream

invariant.statement: Output produced by one tool must never be evaluated as executable code, expressions, queries, or commands by a downstream tool, the agent runtime, or any code path the runtime controls.

claim.statement: If a downstream code path evaluates a tool's output via eval / new Function / exec / SQL string concat / shell -c, then any tool whose output an attacker can influence (RAG corpus, web fetch, filesystem read, another agent's response) becomes a remote-code-execution channel against the host running the agent.

mitigation.summary: Tool outputs are typed data, not code. Downstream dispatch uses a fixed allowlist table indexed by an enum-typed action name. eval / Function / exec are forbidden in the agent runtime, enforced by a lint rule and CI gate. Tool outputs that cross trust boundaries are JSON-parsed in a structured shape and validated against a schema.

references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code
